Der Code liegt jeweils in einer Datei, d: Each code is in a file whose name you have to figure out.
– Passwörter nur mit bcrypt oder Argon2: – Store passwords only with bcrypt or Argon2 (slow, with salt).
– Keine Geheimnisse im Code, keine Klart: – No secrets in code, no plain-text passwords in files.
– Lange Passwörter statt komplizierter R: – Long passwords instead of complicated rules, plus password managers and two-factor.
hashes.txt enthält Hashes verschiedener: hashes.txt contains hashes from different methods, each with a name in front. Wanted: the bcrypt hash. bcrypt always starts with $2a$, $2b$ or $2y$.
Das $ ist in grep ein Sonderzeichen (Zei: In grep, $ is a special character (end of line). With \$ inside single quotes you mean the character itself.
Lösung: grep '\\$2[aby]\\$' hashes.txt |: Solution: grep '\$2[aby]\$' hashes.txt | cut -d: -f1 → cat befunde/neu_bcrypt.txt
Richtig: bcrypt ist langsam und hat eine: Correct: bcrypt is slow and has a salt – good for passwords. Code: {code}
Hashes ohne Kennung erkennt man an der L: You can recognize hashes without a label by their length: MD5 = 32, SHA-1 = 40, SHA-256 = 64 hex characters. Which line is SHA-256?
awk kann die Länge eines Feldes messen:: awk can measure the length of a field: length($2).
Richtig erkannt: 64 Hex-Zeichen = SHA-25: Correctly spotted: 64 hex characters = SHA-256. Code: {code}
alte-db.txt: Benutzer und ungesalzene SH: alte-db.txt: users and unsalted SHA-256 hashes. Two people have the SAME password – you can tell by the identical hash. That is exactly what a salt prevents.
Lösung: cut -d\";\" -f2 alte-db.txt | so: Solution: cut -d";" -f2 alte-db.txt | sort | uniq -d | cut -c1-8 → cat befunde/XXXXXXXX.txt
Zwei Konten, ein Hash – ohne Salt verrät: Two accounts, one hash – without salt, the database gives away identical passwords. Code: {code}
The code is in befunde/FIRST8CHARS.txt – the first 8 characters of the duplicate hash.
test-passwoerter.txt: Beispielpasswörter: test-passwoerter.txt: sample passwords from a training course (made up). How many are SHORTER than 12 characters? The number is the file name.
awk 'length($0)<12' zeigt Zeilen mit wen: awk 'length($0)<12' shows lines with fewer than 12 characters.
Lösung: awk 'length($0)<12' test-passwoe: Solution: awk 'length($0)<12' test-passwoerter.txt | wc -l → cat befunde/NUMBER.txt
Richtig gezählt. Lange Passwörter schlag: Counted correctly. Long passwords beat complicated rules. Code: {code}
Der Quellcode des Bürgerportals liegt un: The source code of the citizen portal is in projekt/. Somewhere there is a password in plain text.
grep -r durchsucht alle Dateien. -i für: grep -r searches all files. -i ignores upper/lower case.
neue-db.txt speichert SALT:HASH, wobei H: neue-db.txt stores SALT:HASH, where HASH = sha256(SALT + password). Which word from the training wordlist woerter.txt belongs to the account "kasse"? This is how admins check for weak default passwords in their OWN database.
Salt und Hash von kasse: grep kasse neue: Salt and hash of kasse: grep kasse neue-db.txt | cut -d: -f2 or -f3
Für jedes Wort w: echo -n \"$S$w\" | sha: For each word w: echo -n "$S$w" | sha256sum – first the salt, directly followed by the word.
Lösung: S=$(grep kasse neue-db.txt | cut: Solution: S=$(grep kasse neue-db.txt | cut -d: -f2); H=$(grep kasse neue-db.txt | cut -d: -f3); for w in $(cat woerter.txt); do echo -n "$S$w" | sha256sum | grep -q $H && echo $w; done → cat befunde/WORD.txt
Standardpasswort gefunden – sofort änder: Default password found – have it changed right away! Code: {code}
Eine (erfundene) Liste geleakter E-Mail-: A (made-up) list of leaked email addresses and the staff list. Who from the administration is in the leak and has to change their password?
Für jede Mitarbeiter-Adresse prüfen, ob: For each staff address, check whether it is in the leak: while read m; do …; done < mitarbeiter.txt
Lösung: while read m; do grep -q \"$m\": Solution: while read m; do grep -q "$m" leak.txt && echo $m; done < mitarbeiter.txt → cat befunde/maNN.txt
Im Leak gefunden: Passwort ändern, Zwei-: Found in the leak: change the password, turn on two-factor. Code: {code}
bcrypt hat einen Kostenfaktor ($2y$12$ =: bcrypt has a cost factor ($2y$12$ = 12). The higher it is, the slower it is for attackers. One account in bcrypt.txt has a factor that is far too low (below 10).
Mit -F'$' trennt awk an den Dollarzeiche: With -F'$' awk splits at the dollar signs. Then field 3 is the cost factor.
Lösung: awk -F'$' '$3<10' bcrypt.txt | c: Solution: awk -F'$' '$3<10' bcrypt.txt | cut -d: -f1 → cat befunde/konto13.txt
Kostenfaktor 4 ist viel zu schnell. Fix:: Cost factor 4 is far too fast. Fix: rehash with at least 12. Code: {code}
